question: The interquartile range excludes _______ of the values.
solution:
The correct answer is **50%.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• The **interquartile range** is a useful measure of variability that is less affected by outliers than the range, which is the difference between the maximum and minimum values in a dataset.
 
• T he IQR is sometimes used to identify outliers, which are values that fall more than 1.5 times the IQR below the first quartile or above the third quartile.
 
• The IQR can be used to define the box in a box plot, which is a graphical representation of the distribution of a dataset.
 
• The whiskers of the box plot extend to the minimum and maximum values within 1.5 times the IQR of the first and third quartiles, respectively.
 
• The IQR can be calculated using the formula IQR = Q3 - Q1, where Q1 and Q3 are the first and third quartiles, respectively.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The** interquartile range**

 
 
• It is a robust measure of variability that is useful for datasets with skewed distributions or outliers.
 
• It is a standard measure of variability that is taught in many introductory statistics courses and is commonly used in research and data analysis.
 
• It is a measure of variability that describes the spread of a dataset by dividing it into quarters.
 
 
• Specifically, the IQR is the difference between the upper quartile (Q3) and the lower quartile (Q1).
 
 
 
 
 
• Q1 represents the 25th percentile, which is the value below which 25% of the data falls, while Q3 represents the 75th percentile, which is the value below which 75% of the data falls.
 
 
• Therefore, the IQR includes the middle 50% of the data, and excludes both the lowest 25% and the highest 25% of the values.
 
 
 
• In summary, the correct answer is that the interquartile range excludes 50% of the values, with the remaining 50% falling within the range.
